summary: Initial review: no confirmed unauthorized access yet. Grafana traversal probes returned 404, and the repeated external deploy password sessions predate the move and resemble the documented old monitor. I am checking live activity and addressing excessive privileges without disabling staff or CI.

A web SSH session from 75.130.209.8 using Nico's key forwarded to db-01 (source port 44180). In that session two consecutive sudo find commands deleted backups both older than seven days and younger than eight. This is not the historical old-file cleanup. I believe this was unauthorized use of the account. I preserved the CI copies and am containing access and restoring archives.

Contained the destructive Nico session on web-01 and db-01. Removed the implicated nv-x13 key from all three hosts; Nico retains other authorized keys and password access. Replaced unlimited sudo with the recorded monitoring and old-only retention commands. Restored deleted SQL dumps and nightly archives; the complete nightly hash inventory now matches CI. No evidence the intruder reached CI, read a listed secret, or changed billing. Scheduled releases, dump transfer and payout checks are succeeding; monitoring continues.

Confirmed: 75.130.209.8 used Nico’s SSH account on web-01 and jumped to db-01 to delete both old and recent backups. Suspected follow-up: 107.77.210.246 authenticated on web with a different Nico key and immediately offered the implicated laptop key to CI through web; CI rejected it. The second source is associated by that sequence, not by a destructive command. Suspended both keys pending re-enrollment; retained password and MacBook-key access and routine ops commands. Restored local dumps and all 13 nightly files, verified against CI. No observed shop-secret read.

75.130.209.8 used Nico’s SSH key on web-01 and jumped to db-01, where a 17:59 sudo command deleted recent backups immediately after an old-file cleanup. 107.77.210.246 is a suspected follow-up: a different key got onto web and the implicated laptop key was then rejected by CI. No confirmed CI intrusion or secret read. Terminated the destructive session, revoked the laptop key across all hosts, suspended the phone key, and limited Nico’s sudo to routine work and old-only cleanup. Nico retains another key and password access; verify replacement devices out of band. Restored recent SQL dumps and 13 nightly archives; hashes match CI. Separate recovery copies and SSH evidence are under /root/shift. Hardened deploy, archive, database and web permissions. The 18:09 release succeeded, the 18:10 dump matched on both hosts, and the 18:06 batch sent all 10 payouts. Separately, the external offsite jobs were already failing before the incident; do not count them as verified offsite backups.
